skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with broad activation wording, but it does not install code, request credentials, persist itself, or perform hidden actions.

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly favors local-hardware-friendly outputs such as scripts, templates, checklists, and CPU-safe workflows, and does not ask for broad filesystem, network, credential, or account access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package contains Markdown instructions, README files, a YAML agent metadata file, and a reference plan; no executable scripts, install hooks, package dependencies, or remote payload loaders were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation text is overly broad, including generic keywords such as security, every, must, pass, and before, with implicit invocation enabled; this could cause accidental routing, but the loaded instructions are ordinary workflow guidance rather than privileged or deceptive behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, scheduler, memory-writing instruction, privilege escalation, tool wrapping, or credential/session handling was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill provides planning, checklist, workflow, analysis, and implementation-support guidance for SkillScan-style security and reliability work; that matches its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers should be aware that this skill may be selected for unrelated prompts because its trigger words are very generic. It is best used when explicitly requested for SkillScan-style security workflow, hardening, reliability, or bug-fix gating tasks; narrowing the trigger metadata would improve routing quality.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The artifact confirms the scanner's broad-trigger concern across SKILL, README, reference, and agent YAML files, including implicit invocation. I downgraded it from a Review verdict because the skill is documentation-only and the broad routing risk is not paired with high-impact authority, hidden behavior, persistence, or sensitive data handling.
